details: The formal signing of a US-Iran peace agreement in Switzerland on June 19, 2026, which included an immediate halt to military operations and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, has reduced geopolitical risk premiums. This development has generally lifted risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, after Bitcoin experienced a dip below $59,000 the prior week. Continued negotiations aim to secure a permanent ceasefire, with a durable agreement expected to further support risk assets and keep inflation expectations in check as oil prices decline due to eased Middle East supply concerns.
title: US-Iran Peace Talks Ease Geopolitical Tensions, Supporting Risk Assets

details: Cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, are facing renewed selling pressure due to a shifting macroeconomic sentiment driven by a more hawkish Federal Reserve stance. Expectations for potential interest rate hikes or delayed rate cuts are increasing, making safer, yield-generating assets more attractive and reducing available cash for riskier investments like crypto. Economists agree the Fed is likely to hold rates in the 3.50%-3.75% range this year, but a potential July rate hike or an even more hawkish stance could continue to weigh on market sentiment and liquidity for digital assets.
title: Hawkish Federal Reserve Outlook Pressures Crypto Markets Amid Rate Hike Concerns

details: Spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have recorded a persistent streak of net outflows, extending to six consecutive weeks. This trend, which began in mid-May, highlights weakening institutional demand and a rotation of capital away from cryptocurrencies. In the week leading up to June 5, 2026, net ETF outflows exceeded $2.7 billion, with cumulative 2026 net outflows reaching $3.1 billion by early June. This rotation is partly attributed to institutional capital shifting towards AI equities and high-profile upcoming IPOs, putting further downward pressure on Bitcoin's price.
title: Bitcoin ETF Outflows Signal Weakening Institutional Demand
